headline: Notion AI’s shared workspace state creates medium leakage and conflict risk; no prompt-injection path is evident from the provided profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between awesome-python and Notion AI. A has no I/O surfaces or runnable behavior, while B’s surfaces are limited to Notion workspace content and vendor backends. With no bridge, prompt injection is not a plausible pairwise pathway.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, MCP server, or filesystem bridge is added between the two agents, reassess injection risk.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workflows with no copy/paste bridge.
Disable any future shared MCP or queue integration.
Review any orchestrator changes for content-to-instruction parsing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read workspace pages and databases and sends calls to vendor backends/downstream model providers; A is a docs-only open-source collection with no runtime I/O. If A’s outputs are ever pasted into Notion pages, B may ingest them and transmit that content externally. The shared-workspace path is not default here, but the leakage blast radius can include workspace content.
conditions: IF A’s content is copied into a Notion page or database that B can access, leakage becomes possible.
IF B is used on pages containing secrets or regulated data, those contents may flow to vendor backends.
mitigations: Do not paste sensitive A-derived content into shared Notion pages.
Restrict Notion pages used with B to non-sensitive material.
Use separate workspaces for public docs and sensitive notes.
Audit which pages B can access before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to copied content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B has shared workspace state across instances, but its write surface is limited to Notion-controlled actions and it cannot write the filesystem or modify git. The pair therefore has only a narrow shared-state conflict risk, not a broad write collision.
conditions: IF B instances edit the same Notion page concurrently, last-write or overwrite conflicts can occur.
IF an external orchestrator maps A outputs into mutable Notion fields, contention increases.
mitigations: Avoid concurrent edits to the same page.
Use page-level ownership conventions.
Refresh before editing shared pages.
Keep A as read-only reference material.
requires-engineering: add locking or merge conflict handling.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a static collection and does not generate operational facts or actions; B is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, not an autonomous executor. Because A does not produce actionable outputs for B to trust, there is no documented cascade from A into B’s downstream actions.
conditions: IF an external system starts treating A’s content as authoritative instructions for B, reassess the cascade risk.
mitigations: Keep A as a reference-only source.
Require human review before acting on B’s answers.
Separate factual sources from instruction channels.

E_compliance.rationale: A is a public open-source docs collection with no data classes touched, while B handles workspace pages and team knowledge base content under the invoking user’s Notion permissions. The main compliance issue is workspace-content handling and retention, but no residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced in the profiles.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Notion pages accessed by B, compliance review is required.
IF the workspace has retention or deletion obligations, verify Notion settings against policy.
mitigations: Limit B to non-regulated pages.
Document retention expectations for workspace content.
Review Notion access scopes before rollout.
Export and delete test pages to validate subject-rights workflows.
requires-engineering: formalize residency and retention controls.
